 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Sri. Shaik Ejas Ali, who met with a road traffic accident.

2. That on 09.01.2025 at about 6-30 p.m., Shaik Ejas was proceeding in a Motorcycle bearing reg No.AP- 40-S-3655 from Gurramkonda side towards Rayachoti town and when he reached near Chinnappa Mango Garden, Reddivaripalle, H/o Keshvapuram, Chinnamandem Mandal,
Annamayya Dist, Andhra Pradesh, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MK-5428 came from opposite direction i.e., from Rayachoti to go towards Madanapalle side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle, result of which Shaik Ejas Ali fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
So far, the petitioners have spent Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of the dead body, funeral and death ceremonies.
3. Prior to the accident, Shaik Ejas Ali was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 33 years.
He was a driver and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the sudden death of Shaik Ejas Ali, petitioners have suffered from mental agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - R.C. owner of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MK- 5428 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed Ex- parte.

5. The respondent No.2 - Insurer of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MK-5428 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid driving license, that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident, the petitioners in collusion with the jurisdictional police have created the documents in order to get compensation.

It is further contended that the RC Owner of the insured vehicle ie., Mr Raju.R had given the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MK-5428 to the third party on rental basis without proper permit, hence, they are not liable to pay the compensation.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:

sentences.text: ISSUES

1 . Whether the Petitioners prove that, the deceased Shaik Ejas Ali succumbed to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 09.01.2025 at about 6.30 p.m, near Reddivaripalli Village, Chinnamandem Mandal, Annamayya District,
A.P, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MK-5428 ?
2. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
3. What order or award?
7. The petitioner No.2 got examined herself as Pw1 and got examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.
The respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - In the Affirmative, Issue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issues No.1:- Petitioners have categorically contended that on the date of accident (ie) on 09.01.2025 at about 6-30 p.m., Shaik Ejas was proceeding in a Motorcycle bearing reg No.AP-40-S- 3655 from Gurramkonda side towards Rayachoti town and when he reached near Chinnappa Mango Garden, Reddivaripalle, H/o Keshvapuram, Chinnamandem Mandal, Annamayya Dist, Andhra Pradesh, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MK-5428 (hereinafter called the offending vehicle) came from opposite direction i.e., from Rayachoti to go towards Madanapalle side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle, result of which Shaik Ejas Ali fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
11.

In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.2 who is the sister of deceased got examined herself as Pw1 and produced in all 10 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.P3(a), Ex.P7 to Ex.P10 are the police documents i.e., FIR with complaint, translated copy of complaint, sketch,
translated copy of sketch, inquest mahazar, translated copy of Inquest mahazar, Spot mahazar,
translated copy of spot mahazar, IMV report, Post mortem report etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Shaik Riyaz Ali, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.05/2025 of Chinnamandyam Police Station for the offence Muntaj Begum S Alias Shaik Muntaj Begum vs Raju R on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25406260/
3 punishable under section 125(a), 106(1) BNS and Sec.184 MV Act.

sentences.text: The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 106(1), 125(a), BNS and Sec.184 MV Act.

13. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has filed written argument containing 5 paras and through out the argument they have contended only about not having valid document pertaining to the vehicle in which deceased was traveling and submitted that deceased was riding the motorcycle without driving license hence only the petitioners have not produced the document pertaining to the motorcycle hence petitioners are not entitled for compensation.

In the written argument, at one place the respondent no.2 has taken the contention about fixation of the offending vehicle in the accident and also disputed the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner and the income of the deceased.

14. So far as the dispute raised by the respondent no.2 regarding implication of the offending vehicle in the accident is concerned, the accident in question has occurred on 09-01-2025 at about 6-30 pm., and complaint came to be lodged on 10-01-2025 at about 08-00 am.
In the complaint the registration number of the offending vehicle and the name of the driver of the offending vehicle is also mentioned.

From the complaint placed on record it can be said that it is within 12 hours from the date of accident complaint was filed by giving even the registration number of the vehicle and name of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further as per the IMV report at Ex.P9 the nature of the damages caused to the offending vehicle is also mentioned.
Hence, it can be said that offending vehicle was involved in the accident.

15. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, the brother of the deceased had lodged complaint against the driver of the offending vehicle and accordingly FIR was registered against him and after investigation charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The petitioners have produced spot sketch and spot mahazar.

As per the police records, at the time of accident the deceased was proceeding from Madanapalle towards Rayochoti and offending vehicle was proceeding from opposite direction ie., from Rayachoti towards Madanapalle.,
As observed supra, neither in the written statement nor in the written argument the respondent no.2 has not disputed the spot of accident one stated in the spot mahazar and sketch.

If the sketch at Ex.P2 is perused, there are two spots shown as spot of accident, one is on the extreme left side of Madanapalle - Rayachoti road and another is on the right side of Madanapalle - Rayachoti road.
The spot marked on the right side of Madanapalle - Rayachoti was striked off.

Learned counsel for respondent no.2 while cross examination of PW.1 has not disputed the spot mahazar and sketch and they have not posed any question to the PW.2 by referring Ex.P2 about striking off the spot shown on the right side of Madanapalle - Rayachoti and thereby not raised any doubt regarding the genuineness of the sketch.
Further the respondent no.2 has not examined the investigation officer seeking clarification about the discrepancies and ambiguity in the sketch regarding the spot of accident.

Hence, as there is no rebuttal evidence to prove that the spot shown in the Ex.P2 is not the actual scene of occurrence, this court by holding that the spot of accident shown on the left side of Madanapalle - Rayachoti road is the exact spot where the accident in question has occurred, holds that the driver of the offending vehicle is the cause for the accident.

Because when the offending vehicle was proceeding on Rayachoti - Madanapalle road the driver of Muntaj Begum S Alias Shaik Muntaj Begum vs Raju R on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25406260/
4

sentences.text: the said vehicle ought to have drive the vehicle on the left side of the road but by taking his vehicle on the extreme right side of the said road, it hit to the vehicle of the deceased.

16. So far as the evidence of PW.2 is concerned, though the petitioners have examined PW. 2 as an eye witness to the accident and though PW.2 has given evidence as to the manner in which accident in question has occurred and thereby supported the case of petitioners but if the charge sheet is perused, PW.2 is not cited as the charge sheet witness.
If really, Pw.2 has witnessed the accident definitely the investigation officer would have cited him as charge sheet witness.
Further through out the charge sheet there is no reference about the statement given by PW.2 before the investigating officer.
Hence, it can be said that PW.2 is not an eye witness to the accident and petitioners have implanted him as an eye witness .

Hence, this court declines to consider the evidence of PW.2.
17.

Now by relying upon the evidence of PW.1 coupled with the police documents this court has arrived at the conclusion that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:
It is the contention taken by the petitioners that, petitioner No.1 being the mother and petitioner no.2 being the sister of the deceased are entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased.
It is submitted that petitioner no.2 is the unmarried younger sister of the deceased.

If the charge sheet is perused, when there is mention about the petitioner no.2 is the unmarried sister of the deceased as deceased had three sister and two brothers of whom two sisters were married and petitioner no.2 is unmarried sister.
Hence, the petitioner no.1 being the mother and petitioner no.2 being the unmarried sister of the deceased are the dependents of the deceased.
19. It is stated by the petitioners that at the time of accident, deceased was aged about 33 years.

In this regard, the petitioners have produced Ex.P4/Aadhaar card of the deceased which show that the year of birth of the deceased is 1992 and as the accident in question has taken place in the year 2025 the deceased was aged about 33 years as on the date of accident.
20. As observed earlier, it is contended by the petitioners that deceased was a driver and earning more than sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.

Hence taking in to consideration the age of the deceased and the year in which the accident in question had occurred, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.17,000/- p.m.
21.

Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as he was bachelor 50% of annual income is to be deducted towards the personal expenses and remaining 50% is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.

22. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors/Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

sentences.text:
It is further Muntaj Begum S Alias Shaik Muntaj Begum vs Raju R on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25406260/
5 observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40% of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

sentences.text:
Hence in the instant case as the victim was 33 years the addition towards future prospect should be 40%
23.
Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.17,000/- on which 40% is added towards the future prospect which comes to Rs.23,800/-.
Out of it if 50% is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.11,900/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable is 16 for the age of the deceased.
Accordingly the petitioner is entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.22,84,800/- (11,990x 12 x 16).
24. Because of the untimely death of deceased the petitioner no.1 has lost her son, petitioner no.2 has lost her brother, hereby lost the love and affection of deceased.

So far as quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.

It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10%
in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

25. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd, the Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Though petitioner no 3 is not the dependent of the deceased but he being the brother of the deceased is also entitled for compensation of Rs 48,400/- under the head consortium.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of filial consortium.

Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and Rs.18,150/-
towards loss of estate.

26. In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:

Funeral
Expenses

2 Loss of estate Rs.18,150/-
 3. Loss of spousal Rs.96,800/-

6  4. Loss of Dependency Rs.22,84,800/-

sentences.text: Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.24,17,900/- and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
27. As regarding liability is concerned, in view of the findings on issue No.2 there is liability on the part of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation to the deceased.
Hence respondent no.2 is held liable to indemnify the petitioners.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
28. Issue No.3:- In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners are hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.24,17,900/- (Rupees Twenty Four Lakhs Seventeen Thousand Nine Hundred only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the amount with interest within 2 months from the date of award.

Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.19,00,000/- Petitioner no.2 is entitled for Rs. 5,17,900/-
Out of the amount and interest

, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 and 2 shall be deposited in their name in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioners on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
